messages:
Maya: heads up, we saw another autoscaler overshoot during the eu-west-1 incident this morning. GPUs spun up, a bunch of pods moved, then nodes went NotReady and CA kept adding more.
Jordan: ugh. root cause known?
Maya: preliminary: MTU mismatch on a new calico peer config + jumbo frames from the on-prem tunnel. saw CUDA driver disconnects in node logs, kubelet flapped, node condition -> NotReady for ~90s.
Edward: CA behavior makes sense: scale-up triggered by pending pods; when nodes go NotReady CA doesn't immediately remove them and keeps scaling because pending pods remain. feedback loop.
Liya: we need to reduce blast radius for tenant workloads. current shared-hosted-pool is single admin pool for many tenants. when one tenant's networking flaps it drags others.
Maya: proposal: ephemeral "burst" nodepools tainted (gpu-burst=true:NoSchedule) and labeled per-tenant. provisioning CRD + CA policy tweaks so ephemeral nodes have different backoff/scale-down.
Jordan: why CRD vs just more nodepools?
Edward: CRD gives lifecycle hooks: ttl, billing tags, pre-delete hooks to flush caches, and allows admission policies to block cross-tenant mounting.
Liya: must avoid cold-start regressions. prefer long-lived pools when pod has model.cache=true or cacheHot annotation.
Maya: CA changes we need:
- notReady age threshold before CA treats node as deletable
- scale-up backoff when NotReady nodes exist
- separate toleration window for burst pools
- annotate nodes provisioning-type=ephemeral

Edward: pre-delete should trigger a cache flush/checkpoint to S3 to avoid long warmups.
Liya: cost accounting: annotate nodes billing:tenant-<id> via mutating webhook so billing can roll up.
sre-oncall-bot: incident: eu-west-1 gpu-nodepool-3 cycling — created 6 new nodes in 12m, recovered after 23m. Alerts: #infra-high-cpu, #kube-notready.
Maya: for network root cause: add calico MTU sanity check in node-init and a preflight in the image.
Jordan: runbook changes:
- if CA spike >3 nodes in 5m: pause CA and alert oncall
- if >1 tenant namespaces evicting simultaneously: escalate as infra network event

Liya: isolation approach: soft isolation (taints+ns selectors) vs hard (per-tenant pools). hybrid: enterprise -> dedicated, standard -> soft-isolated-burst, dev -> shared.
Edward: agree. tiers: enterprise dedicated, standard soft-isolated, dev best-effort.
Maya: impl checklist:
1) CRD: BurstNodePool
2) mutating webhook to stamp nodes
3) CA config tweaks (ignoreNotReadySeconds, scaleDownUnneededTime)
4) node-init MTU check + driver recovery
5) pre-delete cache-flush hook
6) dashboards: per-tenant churn, pending-pod trigger rate, CA actions

Jordan: paste CRD example?
Maya: sure
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood.ai/v1alpha1
kind: BurstNodePool
metadata:
  name: tenant-42-burst
spec:
  tenantId: "tenant-42"
  gpu: nvidia-t4
  minNodes: 0
  maxNodes: 8
  ttlMinutes: 120
  taints:
    - key: "gpu-burst"
      value: "true"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
  labels:
    provisioning-type: ephemeral
    billing: tenant-42
```
Liya: add admission policy to disallow hostPath/privileged on burst nodes.
Edward: also update scheduler predicate to prefer nodes with same model-cache tag when pod annotation model.cache=true.
Jordan: who owns rollout? infra + eng-runtime + billing. canary tomorrow against tenant-42 in eu-west-1.
Maya: filing PR for CRD + webhook, will include metrics + cost tags. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-9821
Jordan: short-term mitigations: bump kubelet eviction thresholds for ephemeral allocations, add CA pause rule, increase CA notReadyGracePeriod to 3m for gpu pools. monitor and abort canary if churn >10%.
Maya: filing tickets and will link PR here.
